dossier.public_summary: The dip depth alternates between shallow and deep every orbit, and between sectors - a planet would always have the same depth. Two especially deep events dominate the signal, and the transit is too long for this small star. Together this is best explained by a nearby or blended eclipsing binary with a 12.6-day period folded at half period, not a 2.25 Earth-radius planet on the target.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by ~factor 4 (775 ppm difference, 6.8 sigma) where a planet must be same - is an eclipsing binary at period_x2 12.6 d, not P=6.29 d. Difference is consistent across sectors (sector_oe_max_sigma 8.47, sector_oe_sectors_over_3 2).
reasons.value: depth_odd_ppm 892.8 vs depth_even_ppm 3968, diff_sigma 6.804, depth_difference 0.775, depth_ratio 4.4

reasons.why: Depth really changes, already present in per-sector data (sectors.p_constant 0.00008132), seen as spikes at 0.125 d phases (sectors 68 and 95) when the true eclipses occur. Not a calibration offset.
reasons.value: verdict changes_within_a_source, p_constant_all 8.250322460890658e-05, sector depths 1810, 913, 3121, 3615 ppm

reasons.why: Single-transit SNR is driven by two anomalously deep outliers; the flat-bottom shape (v_sigma -1.669) is a by-product of fitting highly inconsistent events, not a planet transit.
reasons.value: p_consistent 7.122863808574452e-24, share_of_top_3 0.929, outliers depth_ppm 7994 sigma 7.7 and 6357 sigma 5.1

reasons.why: Duration too long for central transit of this M dwarf (rad 0.4325 Rsun) positively supports a stellar eclipse geometry, consistent with EB.

reasons.why: Independent scorer ranks as only 5% planet-like, consistent with the strong odd-even and depth-instability evidence.
